story:
[emotion:QT/happy] Ethan loved racing toy cars across the big, checkered rug in his room. He was building a three-lane track, but the red ramp kept sliding because the floor was too smooth.

[emotion:QT/angry] "This is really tricky," Ethan said, although he tried three times to fix it.

His neighbor, Charlie, knocked on the door. Charlie saw the crooked ramp right away and thought Ethan looked frustrated. [emotion:QT/angry] "Maybe if we put something thick underneath, it would stay still," Charlie said cheerfully. [emotion:QT/happy] Ethan went to his shelf and gave Charlie a chunky book. Charlie slid it under the ramp while Ethan held the track steady.

"Ready?" Charlie asked, holding a yellow car.

[emotion:QT/happy] "Ready!" Ethan said, grinning.

They took turns racing their cars through the tunnel and down the ramp. After each race, they cheered together because their teamwork had finally made everything work perfectly. [emotion:QT/happy] [gesture:clapping] Ethan felt proud and really happy that Charlie had come over. [emotion:QT/happy]

scenes: Ethan kneeling on a large checkered rug in his room, building a three-lane toy car track with a red ramp that keeps sliding on the smooth floor, looking frustrated.
Charlie standing at the open bedroom door, spotting the crooked ramp, while Ethan looks relieved; Charlie slides a chunky book under the ramp as Ethan holds the track steady.

questions.question: What is the main message of this story about Ethan and his race track?
questions.correct_answer: Teamwork helped them solve a tricky problem
wrong_answers: Racing cars is always easy to do
Charlie was better at building than Ethan

questions.question: What did Charlie think of while Ethan was trying to fix the ramp that kept sliding?
questions.correct_answer: Putting something thick underneath the ramp
wrong_answers: Using tape to hold the ramp still
Moving the track to a different room

questions.question: After Charlie gave the idea, what did Ethan give Charlie so the ramp would stay still?
questions.correct_answer: A chunky book from his shelf
wrong_answers: A yellow toy car from the track

questions.question: Why do you think Ethan felt really proud and happy after Charlie came over to help?
questions.correct_answer: Because their teamwork finally made the race track work
wrong_answers: Because he won every single car race they played
Because Charlie brought him a new three-lane track

questions.question: What do you think would have happened if Charlie had not knocked on the door while Ethan was struggling with the ramp?
questions.correct_answer: Ethan might have stayed frustrated and the ramp would not work
wrong_answers: Ethan would have thought of the book idea by himself right away
The ramp would have stopped sliding on the smooth floor

questions.question: Why was it a good idea for Ethan to let Charlie help with the ramp?
questions.correct_answer: Asking a friend for help makes hard things easier.
wrong_answers: Building a track by yourself is the best way to learn how it works.
Fixing problems quickly means you can play sooner on your own.

questions.question: What did Ethan and Charlie show us by what they did with the cars?
questions.correct_answer: Taking turns makes playing together more fun for everyone.
wrong_answers: Racing as many times as possible helps you get better at the game.
Letting the fastest person go first makes the game more exciting.

questions.question: What is one lesson from this story?
questions.correct_answer: Working together means both of you win.
wrong_answers: Sharing your toys with a neighbor will always fix any problem.
Having the right equipment is the most important part of playing a game.

takeaways: Asking a friend for help makes hard things easier.
Taking turns makes playing together more fun for everyone.
Working together means both of you win.
